query: For a multi-principal element alloy system known for limited ductility in cast forms, propose a processing route and phase constitution that would simultaneously achieve nanocrystalline grain sizes below 50 nm and a dual-phase solid solution structure, thereby enhancing hardness and yield strength without inducing brittle intermetallic formation. Support this hypothesis with prior evidence regarding grain refinement mechanisms and phase stability limits, define the boundary conditions where this microstructure becomes unstable, and suggest a falsification experiment to distinguish this mechanism from simple solid solution strengthening.

generation.hypothesis: Simultaneous nanocrystallization (<50 nm) and dual-phase BCC/B2 solid solution formation in a refractory multi-principal element alloy can be achieved via severe plastic deformation followed by a sub-solvus anneal, provided the alloy composition is tuned to maintain a VEC < 4.6 and atomic size mismatch δ < 6.6% to suppress brittle intermetallics while stabilizing a nanoscale B2 precipitate within a BCC matrix.
generation.material_initial_state: A cast refractory multi-principal element alloy (e.g., NbMoTaW-V or NbMoTaTiW) exhibiting a coarse-grained single-phase BCC structure with limited ductility and low yield strength.
generation.intervention: Apply severe plastic deformation (e.g., High-Pressure Torsion or Cryogenic Rolling) to induce grain refinement to <50 nm, followed by a short-duration annealing treatment at a temperature below the solvus line of the target B2 phase but above the recovery temperature of the BCC matrix.
generation.conditions: Annealing temperature range: 0.4–0.6 Tm (where Tm is the melting point), atmosphere: inert (Ar), holding time: <1 hour to prevent grain coarsening and intermetallic precipitation.
generation.structural_mediator: A nanoscale, coherent or semi-coherent B2 ordered precipitate phase dispersed within a disordered BCC solid solution matrix, stabilized by high configurational entropy and limited atomic diffusion during the short anneal.
generation.mechanism: Grain refinement via severe plastic deformation increases dislocation density and grain boundary area, providing nucleation sites for the B2 phase. The subsequent anneal triggers spinodal decomposition or nucleation of the B2 phase without allowing sufficient time for the formation of brittle, coarse intermetallics (like Laves phases), leveraging the high entropy of mixing to maintain phase stability within the dual-phase regime.
generation.predicted_outcome: A dual-phase microstructure with BCC matrix and nanoscale B2 precipitates (<50 nm) resulting in a yield strength >2000 MPa and hardness >600 Hv, while maintaining ductility >10% due to the suppression of brittle intermetallic networks and the presence of the ductile BCC matrix.
generation.baseline: The cast alloy with coarse grains and single-phase BCC structure, which exhibits low yield strength (<1000 MPa) and brittle failure modes.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis fails if the atomic size mismatch (δ) exceeds 6.6% or the valence electron concentration (VEC) exceeds 4.6, as these conditions favor the formation of brittle intermetallic phases (e.g., Laves or complex tetragonal phases) over the desired BCC/B2 dual-phase solid solution, as noted in thermodynamic criteria for HEA phase formation.
generation.uncertainty: Uncertainty exists regarding the exact annealing temperature window required to nucleate the B2 phase without triggering grain coarsening or intermetallic precipitation, as thermodynamic data for specific refractory HEA systems is limited. Additionally, the stability of the nanocrystalline structure at elevated operating temperatures (>1000 K) is not fully established in the provided evidence.

falsification_experiment.design: Synthesize a series of NbMoTaW-V based alloys with varying VEC (4.4 to 5.0) and δ (5.0% to 7.0%). Subject all samples to identical severe plastic deformation (HPT) to achieve <50 nm grains, followed by a standardized anneal at 0.5 Tm for 30 minutes. Analyze the resulting microstructure using TEM and XRD.
measurements: Phase identification and volume fraction (XRD, TEM)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis is falsified if samples with VEC > 4.6 or δ > 6.6% fail to form the dual-phase BCC/B2 structure and instead exhibit brittle intermetallic phases (e.g., Laves) with ductility < 5%, or if samples with VEC < 4.6 and δ < 6.6% fail to form the B2 phase or exhibit grain coarsening > 100 nm after annealing.

cited_evidence.text: Abstract Concurrent strength–ductility improvement of HfMoTaTiZr is achieved via Cr addition and the underlying strengthening mechanism was discussed. 4.2 at% Cr addition into HfMoTaTiZr led to the formation of a Laves phase, in addition to the BCC phase. The hardness of HfMoTaTiZrCr 0.5 is 535.8 Hv 0.3 , 56.96% higher than the reference alloy HfMoTaTiZr. The yield strength and fracture strain of HfMoTaTiZrCr 0.5 reach 1750.6 ± 80.3 MPa and 14.0 ± 2.9%, respectively, 207.5 MPa and 20.6% higher than HfMoTaTiZr. Solid solution hardening and the presence of the intermetallic Laves phase are believed to be responsible for the enhancement in strength and the formation of a reticulated structure of the Laves phase in HfMoTaTiZrCr 0.5 results in the improvement in ductility.

Abstract A NbMoTaWVTi refractory high entropy alloy (HEA) has been successfully synthesized by mechanical alloying (MA) and spark plasma sintering (SPS). The microstructure and mechanical properties of this alloy are investigated. It is observed that only two types of body-centered cubic (BCC) solid solutions are formed in the powders after ball milling for 40 h. However, a new face-centered cubic (FCC) precipitated phase is observed in the BCC matrix of bulk material consolidated by SPS. The FCC precipitated phase is identified as TiO, due to the introduction of O during the preparing process of HEA. The compressive yield strength, fracture strength, and total fracture strain of the consolidated bulk HEA are 2709 MPa, 3115 MPa, and 11.4%, respectively. The excellent mechanical properties can be attributed to solid solution strengthening and grain boundary strengthening of the fine-grained BCC matrix, as well as the precipitation strengthening owing to the formation of TiO particles. Keywords: refractory high entropy alloy, microstructure, mechanical properties

While the AlCoFeNi high entropy alloy exhibits a single ordered B2 phase at high temperature, both the substitution of ferromagnetic Co with antiferromagnetic Cr, and lower annealing temperatures lead to a tendency for this system to decompose into a two-phase mixture of ordered B2 and disordered BCC solid solution. The length scale of this decomposition is determined by the combination of composition and annealing temperature, as demonstrated in this investigation by comparing and contrasting AlCoFeNi with the AlCo 0.5 Cr 0.5 FeNi alloy. The resulting phase stability has been rationalized based on solution thermodynamic predictions. Additionally, it is shown that replacement of Co by Cr in the AlCoFeNi alloy resulted in a substantial reduction in saturation magnetization and increase in coercivity. The microhardness is also strongly influenced by the composition and the length scale of B2 + BCC decomposition in these high entropy alloys.

One of the most promising and progressive fields in modern material science is high-entropy alloys (HEAs). The first to propose HEAs’ concept was J.W. Yeh [ [1] ], but since then, it has changed rather significantly, especially during the last few years [ [2] ]. Due to their extremely high mechanical and physical properties, refractory HEAs are classified as a separate group of materials. Such alloying compositions mainly include elements from the IV, V, and VI columns of the periodic table with some additions of Al, Si, Ni, or Co [ [3] ].

First high-entropy equiatomic compositions based on refractory elements, such as NbMoTaW and NbMoTaWV, were obtained in prior research [ [4] , [5] ]. It was found that the alloys possess higher mechanical properties at higher temperatures in comparison to conventional superalloys, such as Inconel 718 and Haynes 230 [ [6] ]. It was also determined that the addition of V increases the hardness significantly (up to 11.4 GPa at 1150 °C) [ [7] ] and yield strength σ 0.2 from 1058 MPa to 1246 MPa [ [5] ].
